text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Kenya Commercial Bank is under pressure to use its staff pension fund to buy a worthless piece of rocky land in the outskirts of Nairobi at 260 million shillings.
- Four armed gangsters raid a Mombasa casino, escaping with more than three million shillings in local currency and dollars.
- Police arrest a Nairobi businessman and recover 1.4 million shillings believed to be part of 96 million stolen from the Standard Chartered Bank in February.
- Police launch investigations into a lesbian sex syndicate involving schoolchildren.
- The mother and brother of the late University of Nairobi student leader Solomon Muruli undergoes a blood test to determine their genetic relationship with the deceased.
- The government concedes that some of the foreign lawyers hired to work in the attorney-general's chambers had abandoned their jobs.
- A bank analyst is arrested by police investigating the 96 million shillings robbery at Standard Chartered bank.
- At least 1.5 million school-age children are out of school -- either at home or in the streets.
- Nairobi City Mayor Dick Waweru sneaks into the country through Moi International Airport in Mombasa. ($1=55 Kenyan shillings)
